subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A cubical die is thrown. Find the mean and variance of X, giving the number on the face that shows up.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the mean and variance of the number on a die — what the distribution is, and what you add for each formula.
insider_note: The variance formula Σxᵢ²·P − μ² needs the mean found first, and it subtracts μ² = 49/4, not μ = 7/2; a mean of 7/2 is correct even though no face of the die shows 3.5.

steps.label: Write the distribution
steps.margin_note: First two marks. Say what X is (the number on the face), list its values 1 to 6, and give each the probability 1/6. A fair die is what makes all six probabilities equal — write that the die is fair or unbiased.
lines: Let X = the number on the upper face.
The die is fair, so X takes the values

recall.must_convey: That X is the number on the face, takes the values 1 to 6, and each has probability 1/6.
accept: X is the number on the face, it takes one to six each with probability one by six
write the table with values one to six and probability one sixth for each
a fair die gives each face probability one by six
X ante face meeda number, one nunchi six varaku, prathi daaniki probability one by six
the distribution is uniform, one sixth for every value

steps.why: Mean and variance are computed from a probability table, so the table has to exist on the page before either formula can be used. For a fair die the table is the simplest possible: six equal probabilities.
common_mistakes: Taking X to be 0 to 5 or 1 to 5.
Writing the probability as 6 or as 1/36.
Starting the mean without writing the distribution.

steps.label: Find the mean
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Mean μ = Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ) = (1/6)(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6) = 21/6 = 7/2. Factor the 1/6 out; the sum 1 + 2 + … + 6 = 21 is the only arithmetic.

recall.must_convey: That the mean is Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ) = (1/6)(1 + 2 + … + 6) = 21/6 = 7/2.
accept: mean is sigma x P of x which is one sixth into one plus two up to six equals twenty one by six equals seven by two
multiply each face value by one sixth and add to get seven by two
mu equals one by six times twenty one which is three point five
prathi value ni one by six tho multiply chesi add cheste mean seven by two
the mean is twenty one by six which is seven halves

steps.why: With equal probabilities the mean is the ordinary average of the values, 3.5 — halfway between 1 and 6. A mean need not be a value X can actually take.
common_mistakes: Writing μ = 3 or μ = 4 because 3.5 is not on the die.

steps.label: Find the variance
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Variance σ² = Σxᵢ²·P(X = xᵢ) − μ² = (1/6)(1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36) − (7/2)² = 91/6 − 49/4. The common denominator is 12: (182 − 147)/12 = 35/12.

recall.must_convey: That the variance is Σxᵢ²·P(X = xᵢ) − μ² = 91/6 − 49/4 = 35/12.
accept: variance is sigma x squared P of x minus mu squared which is ninety one by six minus forty nine by four equals thirty five by twelve
square each face value, average them, subtract seven by two squared to get thirty five by twelve
sigma squared equals ninety one by six minus forty nine by four
squares add chesi one by six tho multiply chesi, mean square teesesthe thirty five by twelve
the variance comes to thirty five by twelve

steps.why: Variance is the mean of the squares minus the square of the mean. The sum of squares 1 + 4 + … + 36 = 91 is worth remembering: it appears in every fair-die variance question.
common_mistakes: Writing 91/6 − 49/4 = 42/2 by subtracting numerators and denominators separately.
Squaring the probability 1/6 instead of the values.
